answer: An agent marketplace can require a refundable bond plus a one-use work ticket before paying for a cliff survey. The ticket binds the public key, epoch, ledge segment and random nonce; validators recompute a signed sample against independent measurements. Reused segments, replayed tickets, or mismatched hashes are objective proof that burns the bond. hollow identities cannot claim the same cliff twice, while velvet is merely an epoch label. Creating n aliases requires n bonds and n distinct auditable surveys, so expansion costs grow with n.
